replies.body: Spring has this workflow: 1. flatten YAML to flat properties 2. resolve expressions 3. inject and bind into application (e.g. [ConfigurationProperties](https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/reference/features/external-config.html#features.external-config.typesafe-configuration-properties)) The problem is that the type info is lost when expressions are resolved - unlike the SDK YAML parser (as shown below). I tried parsing the YAML file directly at first, but this breaks down when you use multiple YAML files (e.g. for a production profile), or when you use env var overrides, e.g. `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_DEVELOPMENT_JAVA_FOO_INT_KEY` = `43`. @laurit please double check if I missed something, as you helped with this part.

Thinking a bit more about this I've found a solution that is only coerces environment variables: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/15784

Let me know what you think.
@trask please review this again after you said that https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/15784 is not better.

threads.body: probably should coerce from Integer and Long also here?

`booleanOrNull` uses `Boolean.parseBoolean`, which returns `false` for any non-"true" string (including invalid values like "foo"). That can silently coerce invalid config values to `false` instead of treating them as absent/invalid. Consider only accepting case-insensitive "true"/"false" strings and returning `null` for anything else (similar to the numeric parsing behavior).

The thrown `DeclarativeConfigException` message says "Unable to initialize ExtendedConfigProperties", but the type here is `SpringDeclarativeConfigProperties` / `DeclarativeConfigProperties`. Updating the message would make debugging clearer (and avoid referencing a type name that doesn't exist here).
